title: The Navigator's Blind Spot
logline: A celebrated retired jump cartographer is accused of senile incompetence after recent gate calculations cause near-collisions, unaware that a nearby micro-pulsar is warping local spacetime.

roles.description: Legendary stellar cartographer; dignified, terrified of cognitive decline, defending fifty years of unblemished jump tables.
Chief of the jump navigation guild; brisk, protective of corporate transit contracts, eager to retire the legend quietly.
The interstellar pilots' and cartographers' guild licensing jump route ephemerides.
The quiet orbital archive where brass stellar astrolabes and master navigation chronometers are calibrated.
A deep-system radio telescope platform monitoring pulsar timing anomalies and gravitational shifts.

public_situation: Freighter convoys report near-miss navigational divergences as {role:navigators_guild} convenes a tribunal to decertify {role:retired_navigator}.
private_truth: The navigator's calculations are mathematically flawless; an uncatalogued micro-pulsar's frame dragging is introducing microsecond temporal offsets into jump arrivals.

beats.public_change: Notice boards at {role:guild_sanctum} announce that all jump clearances calculated by {role:retired_navigator} are suspended pending psychological review.

missions.reason: She hires an independent pilot to courier her handwritten celestial ephemeris logs to the deep-system radio observatory for peer verification.
missions.private_fact: She privately fears she is losing her mind and spent two sleepless nights re-checking manual logarithm scrolls by hand.

beats.public_change: Deep radio arrays at {role:solar_observatory} detect rhythmic high-energy radio pulses sweeping across the jump gate corridor.

missions.reason: Scan the pulsar's relativistic radio telemetry to compare arrival timestamps against the guild's atomic clock beacon.
missions.private_fact: The telemetry demonstrates that the clocks, not her math, are lagging due to gravitational frame dragging.

beats.public_change: A high-frequency freight convoy emerges from jump fifteen seconds off-target, nearly colliding with an orbital docking ring.

missions.reason: Mine and deliver high-purity cuprite ore to fabricate shielding for the observatory's atomic clock synchronizer array.
missions.private_fact: The guild overseer already knows about the pulsar's interference but suppressed it to avoid paying compensation for delayed convoys.

beats.public_change: The guild tribunal gathers at {role:guild_sanctum} to strip the navigator of her ceremonial sextant and pension.

missions.reason: Deliver the verified relativistic telemetry and cuprite clock readings directly to the tribunal podium before the vote concludes.
missions.private_fact: A corporate freight consortium offered the navigator an unpublicized pension if she accepts blame without releasing the data.

player_choice.prompt: The pilot holds absolute proof that the navigational error is an uncatalogued astronomical phenomenon rather than human failure.

options.label: Present the data to the open tribunal, clearing the navigator and forcing the guild to adjust all gate timing intervals
Deliver the proof privately to the overseer in exchange for an honorary lifetime retirement package for the navigator
Sell the pulsar timing equations to private freight runners who can use the lag to front-run exchange rates

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot presents the pulsar timing proof at the public tribunal.
resolutions.summary: The relativistic anomaly is confirmed. {role:retired_navigator}'s honour and pension are restored, while {role:navigators_guild} widens jump clearance windows.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot proved an old cartographer's jump math was right all along, forcing a proud guild to heed a pulsing star.

resolutions.reached_by: The navigator accepts an opulent private pension in exchange for keeping the guild's timing delays confidential.
resolutions.summary: {role:retired_navigator} steps down with an honorary pension and full honors. {role:navigators_guild} avoids scandal, adjusting routes under the table.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot sells the micro-pulsar timing offsets to private high-frequency cargo syndicates.
resolutions.summary: Private haulers exploit the timing lag to front-run jump markets. {role:retired_navigator} retires in obscurity, while orbital exchanges suffer volatile spikes.

resolutions.reached_by: The proof is lost or the observatory arrays fail to synchronize.
resolutions.summary: The tribunal strips {role:retired_navigator} of her credentials. The timing lag remains unsolved, causing recurring freighter collisions across {role:guild_sanctum}.

loose_threads.detail: The replacement atomic clock module at the guild sanctum carries calibration slips stamped sixty days prior to delivery.
Forward insurance contracts for high-speed jump freighters jumped twenty percent before the navigational tribunal was announced.
Guild clerks mention an unfiled astrophysical memo advising transit managers to widen gate safety intervals by two minutes.

radio_hooks: Navigators guild reviews jump convergence timing tolerances following outer gate incident.
Astrophysicists track subtle relativistic pulsation shifts from nearby micro-pulsar.
Freight dispatchers report three-minute divergence in standardized transponder timestamps.

voice_direction.retired_navigator: Precise, fragile, and fiercely proud. Speaks in immaculate astronomical units and pauses to compose herself whenever memory lapses are implied.
voice_direction.guild_overseer: Polished, hurried, and patronizing. Uses corporate reassurance to mask a ruthless determination to prevent cargo schedule delays.
